query:
title: ARM signoff before Go breaking-change review

question: I'm requesting Go SDK breaking-change approval for my ARM specification change, but ArmSignOff approval is still pending. Which approval should I obtain first?
ground_truth: Obtain ArmSignOff approval first, then request review of the Go SDK breaking changes. In this review workflow, ARM signoff is a prerequisite to that review, not a substitute for the Go decision.

query:
title: Approved development-branch changes

question: My Go reviewers approved a set of breaking specification changes because they target our development branch. They also explicitly said they would add suppression for this approved change and that further changes to the associated release branch would not need another approval. Do I need to request approval again for that covered follow-up?
ground_truth: No. For the development/release-branch work explicitly covered by that reviewer decision, follow the stated suppression and no-further-approval arrangement. The reviewers approved the development-branch changes and included the associated release-branch follow-ups in their waiver. This is a scoped decision, not a general waiver for other branches or unrelated changes.

query:
title: Re-run Go validation after a fix

question: I've fixed the issue that blocked my specification's Go SDK validation. How do I request a fresh Go validation run without changing the specification again?
ground_truth: Comment /azp run SDK Validation - Go on the specification change. This reruns the Go validation check; rerunning an SDK Validation check also re-evaluates SDK Validation Status.

expected_references.title: SDK Validation: re-run checks and re-evaluate status

testcase: Go operation rename preserves HTTP but breaks callers
query:
title: Keep the released Go operation name

question: I renamed our TypeSpec operation from updateTags to update without changing its PATCH URI or method. My released Go SDK loses UpdateTags. Is that a client breaking change, and how can I retain the old Go name?
ground_truth: Yes. Removing UpdateTags breaks existing Go callers even when the HTTP method and URI stay the same. In client.tsp, apply a Go-scoped name to the current TypeSpec operation, for example @@clientName(update, "updateTags", "go"), qualified with its actual namespace or interface. Regenerate and confirm that UpdateTags is retained. Target the TypeSpec operation, not the generated Go method.

expected_references.title: Go breaking changes: operation name changes

query:
title: Correct an erroneous string property to boolean

question: My specification incorrectly modeled a property as a string enum, but the service has always returned a JSON boolean. The feature is not GA and has no live consumers. We've explained why preserving the old type would misrepresent the wire contract and presented the SDK mitigations; the Go reviewer approved the change. Should I retain the string type anyway?
ground_truth: No. In this scoped case, proceed with the approved boolean correction rather than preserve a string contract the service never implemented. Keeping the enum for an older API version would still fail to deserialize the actual boolean. The exported Go type change is source-breaking, but the reviewer accepted it with the stated pre-GA, no-live-consumer context and mitigations. That approval does not make every specification bug fix automatically acceptable.

expected_references.title: Go breaking changes: property type changes

query:
title: Model SKU values that can grow

question: I'm defining our Azure API's SKU as enum Sku { Small, Large }, but we expect more string values later. What TypeSpec shape should I use instead?
ground_truth: Use an extensible union, for example union Sku { Small: "Small", Large: "Large", string }. The base string variant permits future values. Azure core's no-enum guidance explains that TypeSpec enums are closed and adding values in later API versions is breaking. Enums remain allowed for versioning; suppress the rule only for inherently immutable value sets.

expected_references.title: Azure core no-enum rule and suppression guidance

query:
title: Package-name review still has comments

question: I'm trying to release our Go module, but its package-name review still has outstanding naming-cleanup comments. My build checks are green. What should I finish before asking for approval?
ground_truth: Address the outstanding naming-cleanup comments and return the updated result to the reviewer. Those comments must be resolved before package-name approval; green build checks do not resolve the naming concerns.

query:
title: Preserve released Go field casing

question: I renamed a TypeSpec property from oldName to newName while leaving its wire name unchanged. Our stable Go struct loses OldName and gains NewName. How can I keep the exported field our callers already use?
ground_truth: An exported field rename breaks field access even when the wire name is unchanged. In client.tsp, target the current source property with a Go-scoped name, for example @@clientName(MyModel.newName, "oldName", "go"). Regenerate and verify that the public Go field remains OldName.

expected_references.title: Go breaking changes: property name changes

query:
title: Check Go module release readiness

question: I'm preparing our Go SDK for release after API review. Which repository checklist should I use before starting release preparation?
ground_truth: Use the Go release checklist: remove go.mod replace directives, include a LICENSE, document public methods and types, check links and samples, prepare release notes and the changelog, document how to enable logging in the README troubleshooting section, and cover champion scenarios with getting-started guidance. Complete the checklist before the release process.

query:
title: Make an acronym-casing fix durable

question: My reviewer found an acronym-casing issue in our generated Go SDK. I changed the .go file, but regeneration discarded my fix. Where should I correct the name?
ground_truth: Make the customization in the TypeSpec project's client.tsp, then regenerate the SDK and send the corrected output back for review. For a naming override, use the supported Go-scoped clientName customization on the actual source symbol. Do not edit generated Go output as the durable fix: regeneration overwrites it.

expected_references.title: Generate a Go SDK: TypeSpec customization and regeneration

query:
title: Find the inner Go generation error

question: My Go SDK validation summary only says generation failed. Where can I find the detailed error before deciding whether to change my model?
ground_truth: Open the validation check's Pipeline result link to the Azure DevOps run, select the error entry, and expand the log group immediately above the error-summary group. That is where the SDK Validation guide directs you to inspect detailed generation errors. Use the concrete diagnostic rather than guessing a model fix from the summary.

expected_references.title: SDK Validation: detailed SDK generation errors

query:
title: Checkout failure before Go generation

question: My Go validation fails with "core.repositoryformatversion does not support extension: worktreeconfig", followed by a missing generateOutput.json. Several unrelated services are affected, and the engineering-system owners have confirmed a shared checkout incident. What should I do once they apply the fix?
ground_truth: Rerun validation after the infrastructure fix; this is not a reason to change your API model. In the reported incident, owners reran affected validations. In a related follow-up, an expert advised retriggering checks after the known issue was fixed, and the author subsequently confirmed Go validation passed. If a private repository still fails, check with the owners whether it also needs the synchronization that resolved the private-repository instance. The matching error alone does not prove a new failure has that historical cause.

testcase: Go release preparation changes must merge
query:
title: Release preparation changed our changelog

question: I ran Prepare-Release.ps1 for our Go module, and it updated the version and CHANGELOG.md. Can I start the release pipeline with those edits only in my local checkout?
ground_truth: No. The Go release process says changes made by eng/common/scripts/Prepare-Release.ps1 must be committed and merged before continuing. Complete those preparation changes first, then run the internal release pipeline.

expected_references.title: Releasing Go packages: release process, step 2

query:
title: Confirm a Go module release is available

question: I've triggered the release pipeline for our Go module. How do I confirm the intended version is actually available to customers rather than just assume the trigger published it?
ground_truth: Verify the exact module and version, not just the pipeline trigger. The Go release process calls for go get <module>@<version> and checking that pkg.go.dev has updated to the released version. In the channel's release follow-up, the expert confirmed the actual published module version when explaining that release was already complete.

expected_references.title: Releasing Go packages: publication validation, step 4

query:
title: Can I reuse azidentity dependency exceptions?

question: I'm adding github.com/google/uuid to a new Go SDK module outside azidentity. I saw that dependency in the repository's azidentity exceptions. Does that entry permit my module to reference it directly too?
ground_truth: No. The go.mod standards list github.com/google/uuid as an additional dependency for azidentity, specifically for a test; it is not in the general third-party allowlist. That package-specific entry does not authorize a direct reference from your different module. Keep your change within the applicable standards rather than treating another module's exception as a general allowance.

expected_references.title: Go module standards: general allowlist and azidentity exceptions

testcase: Go deprecation release before code deletion
query:
title: Deprecate a module with a replacement

question: I'm retiring our Go module in favor of a stable replacement. Can I delete its code immediately, or what does the Go deprecation guide require first?
ground_truth: Follow the documented deprecation lifecycle. Create MIGRATION.md in the new module, then publish a final patch of the old module with migration instructions in a // Deprecated: go.mod comment, CHANGELOG.md, and the README notice. Update references and request pkg.go.dev removal after that release; this does not stop go get from accessing the module. The guide puts code deletion after an appropriate deprecation period, at least 12 months, with migration time, usage, and replacement-readiness checks.

expected_references.title: Deprecating Go modules: deprecation process, steps 1-5

testcase: Go spec to consumable SDK workflow
query:
title: Consume a new API version through Go

question: I've added a new management-plane API version to our service specification. Where can I find the Go work needed to turn that into a consumable SDK release?
ground_truth: Follow the management-plane SDK release process rather than stop at the specification change. The public Go management SDK release guideline covers updating an existing resource provider or onboarding a new service, generating code, completing checks and review, and release preparation. The Go generation guide describes the TypeSpec/tsp-client workflow, and the release guide covers publishing and verifying the module version.

expected_references.title: Go management SDK release guideline: release process
Generate a Go SDK: TypeSpec and tsp-client

testcase: Go conditional acceptance of newer-language API design
query:
title: New major Go SDK API direction

question: I'm designing a new major version of our Go SDK with generic item operations, lazy decoding, and generic query paging instead of the provisional byte-oriented APIs. If the required newer compiler supports this design, is raising the minimum Go version a reasonable direction?
ground_truth: Yes, conditionally: the owner feedback accepted this direction assuming it is a net win for the codebase's longevity. That is acceptance of the proposed design tradeoff, not proof that any particular future compiler feature has shipped or a blanket policy for every SDK. Establish the actual compiler requirement separately before implementing the proposal.
